CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT DETAILS
Patient Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Sample Type: Fetal tissue
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Prenatal testing for fetal abnormalities. Follow-up testing of solid tissue sample.

TEST PERFORMED
Array Comparative Genomic Hybridization (Array CGH)

METHODOLOGY
Array CGH analysis was performed using a custom-designed oligonucleotide array platform with a median resolution of 120kb. Data analysis was conducted using genomic workbench software with reference to the GRCh37/hg19 human genome assembly.

Supplementary testing:
- QF-PCR analysis performed to exclude triploidy
- Microsatellite analysis performed to confirm sample identity

RESULTS
Array CGH Result: arr(1-22,X)x2

Interpretation: Normal female chromosome complement

No copy number imbalances detected in:
- Chromosomes 1-22 and X
- Known microdeletion/microduplication syndrome regions
- No clinically significant imbalances >0.4Mb identified

Higher resolution re-analysis was performed focusing on regions of known pathogenicity associated with fetal abnormalities. No smaller imbalances of clinical significance were detected.

QF-PCR: Normal female pattern, no evidence of triploidy
Microsatellite analysis: Sample identity confirmed

CONCLUSION
The array CGH analysis shows a normal female chromosome complement with no detectable genomic imbalances. These results do not identify a genetic cause for the reported fetal abnormalities.

LIMITATIONS
Array CGH cannot detect:
- Balanced chromosomal rearrangements
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)
- Point mutations or small insertions/deletions
- Methylation abnormalities or uniparental disomy
- Imbalances smaller than the resolution of this array

SAMPLE STORAGE
The fetal tissue sample will be stored in the laboratory for 12 weeks from the date of this report before disposal. Please contact the laboratory if further testing is required within this timeframe.

Reported by: [redacted name]
Consultant Clinical Scientist
Authorised by: [redacted name]
Consultant Clinical Geneticist
